nodes.name: Insert Keywords History
nodes.notes: Runs BEFORE Get Recently Posted (sequential, not parallel) so that this run's rows are guaranteed to exist -- with their DB id -- by the time Pick Next Keyword looks them up.

nodes.name: Get Recently Posted
nodes.notes: Fetches ALL rows -- both the cooldown filtering and today's row-id lookup happen in the next Code node, to avoid depending on Supabase filter-param schema (which varies by n8n version).

nodes.name: IF New Keyword Found
nodes.notes: true -> a new keyword was found, proceed to approval. false -> every top-20 trend is still on cooldown (or the insert silently failed) -- notifies instead of ending this schedule run with zero trace.

parameters.text: ={{ $json.reason === 'low_volume' ? '이번 회차(3시간 주기)에는 검색 볼륨(1000+) 조건을 만족하는 키워드가 없어 건너뜁니다.' : '이번 회차(3시간 주기)에는 새로 포스팅할 트렌드 키워드가 없어 건너뜁니다.\n(상위 20개 키워드가 모두 최근 14일 내 처리된 상태이거나, 키워드 저장 과정에 문제가 있을 수 있습니다.)' }}

nodes.name: Send Telegram Keyword Approval
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: this inlineKeyboard structure matches n8n's Telegram node UI-driven format, but field names can still shift between versions. If buttons don't render after import, open Reply Markup and confirm the two buttons + their URL values are intact. NOTE: once a retry fires, only the LATEST message's buttons are valid -- earlier messages' buttons point to a superseded wait instance.

nodes.name: Wait Keyword Approval
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: open this node, confirm Resume=On Webhook Call, then toggle 'Limit Wait Time' ON, Limit Type=After Time Interval, and check the Amount field accepts the expression above (switch it to expression/fx mode if it was imported as a plain number).

nodes.name: IF Approval Retry
nodes.notes: true -> loops back to Keyword Approval Attempt with attempt+1. false here means outcome was 'rejected' -- now notifies via Telegram: Keyword Rejected instead of ending silently.

nodes.name: Get Rows For Approval Lookup
nodes.notes: Fetches all rows -- filtering to the pending one happens in the next Code node, same pattern as Get Recently Posted.

nodes.name: Resolve Pending Approval
nodes.notes: Same mechanism as the inline keyboard buttons (a GET to $execution.resumeUrl), just triggered from a typed reply instead of a button click. If this errors, most likely the Wait instance already resumed (button was clicked first) or the retry loop moved past it -- a failure here just means the message came too late.

parameters.text: ={{ $('Find Pending Resume URL').first().json.decision === 'approve' ? '✅ 코멘트 반영해서 초안 작성을 진행할게요.' : '❌ 거절 처리했습니다.' }}{{ $('Find Pending Resume URL').first().json.comment ? '\n\n남기신 코멘트: ' + $('Find Pending Resume URL').first().json.comment : '' }}

nodes.name: Search Naver News
nodes.notes: sort=date so the most recent articles come first, required for the recency filter next. VERIFY IN UI: re-enter your real X-NCP-APIGW-API-KEY-ID/SECRET here after import -- the committed JSON keeps placeholders since this repo is public.

nodes.name: IF News Found
nodes.notes: Moved to run directly off Parse & Split Articles's always-present single item (instead of after Insert News/Aggregate News), so the 'no recent news' branch fires reliably even when count is 0 -- previously zero articles meant Insert News/Aggregate News never ran at all, silently killing this check and the Telegram notification below.

nodes.notes: Same inlineKeyboard structure as the other approval node -- verify buttons survive import. Once a retry fires, only the LATEST message's buttons are valid.

nodes.name: Store Pending Resume URL

nodes.name: IF News Retry
nodes.notes: true -> loops back to News Review Attempt with attempt+1. false means outcome was 'rejected' -> Telegram: News Review Rejected.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens: 4096, tools: [{ name: "blog_draft", description: "워드프레스에 바로 등록 가능한 블로그 초안 생성", input_schema: { type: "object", properties: { title: { type: "string" }, body_html: { type: "string" }, excerpt: { type: "string" }, tags: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }, category: { type: "string", enum: ["정치", "경제", "사회", "생활/문화", "IT/과학", "연예", "스포츠", "국제", "기타"] }, meta_description: { type: "string" }, image_keywords: { type: "string" } }, required: ["title", "body_html", "excerpt", "tags", "category", "meta_description", "image_keywords"] } }], tool_choice: { type: "tool", name: "blog_draft" }, messages: [{ role: "user", content: (() => { const base = `지금 화제인 키워드: ${$('Build News Summary').first().json.keyword} 관련 뉴스: ${$('Build News Summary').first().json.news_list} Google Trends 원본 링크: ${$('Build News Summary').first().json.trend_link} 위 내용을 참고해서 이 키워드를 자연스럽게 다루는 한국어 블로그 글을 작성해줘. 작성 지침: - 도입부는 '~가 화제인 이유는', '~에 대해 알아보겠습니다' 같은 상투적이고 AI스러운 문장으로 시작하지 마. 매번 다른 각도로 -- 최근 반응, 지금 분위기, 사람들이 주목하는 포인트 등 -- 자연스럽게 짚으면서 이 키워드로 시작해줘. 매 포스팅마다 도입부 스타일을 다르게 해줘. - body_html 끝부분은 부가 설명이 아니라 글의 흐름을 자연스럽게 마무리하는 문단으로 끝내고, 참고한 뉴스 출처 링크를 그 안에 자연스럽게 언급해줘. - excerpt는 워드프레스 발췌문(글 목록/공유 시 노출)으로 쓸 1~2문장짜리 짧고 흥미로운 요약을 작성해줘. - meta_description은 본문에는 노출되지 않는 검색엔진용 요약(150자 내외)으로 따로 작성해줘. excerpt와는 톤이 달라도 돼. - category는 정치/경제/사회/생활문화/IT과학/연예/스포츠/국제/기타 중 이 포스팅에 가장 맞는 하나로 골라줘. - image_keywords는 이 글의 대표 이미지를 무료 스톡 사진 사이트(Pexels)에서 검색할 때 쓸 2~4개의 영어 단어야. 이 포스팅의 핵심 소재/키워드와 시각적으로 실제 연관된 장면을 표현해줘 (카테고리 수준의 뭉뚱그린 단어 말고, 이 기사가 다루는 대상·장소·상황을 구체적으로). 단, Pexels는 실존 인물 이름이나 한국 고유명사로는 검색이 안 되니, 그런 경우 그 인물/사안이 속한 상황을 묘사하는 일반적인 영어 단어로 바꿔서 표현해줘 (예: '손흥민 부상' -> 'soccer player injury field', '비트코인 급등' -> 'cryptocurrency finance chart growth', 'OO아파트 붕괴' -> 'apartment building collapse construction'). - body_html 안에는 태그나 '[사진: ...]', '(이미지: ...)' 같은 이미지 자리표시·캡션을 절대 넣지 마. 대표 이미지는 이 워크플로우가 별도로 자동 첨부하니, 본문은 순수 텍스트(문단과 필요한 경우 소제목 정도)로만 작성해줘. - 절대 뉴스 기사를 단순히 요약만 하지 마. 이 사안이 왜 지금 화제인지에 대한 배경, 앞으로 어떻게 흘러갈지에 대한 전망, 비슷한 과거 사례와의 비교, 이게 독자에게 왜 중요한지 같은 너만의 관점과 분석을 최소 한두 문단 이상 담아줘. 기사 내용을 재배열한 것처럼 읽히면 안 되고, 읽고 나서 뭔가 새로운 통찰을 얻었다는 느낌이 들어야 해.`; const comment = $('Evaluate News Review').first().json.comment; return comment ? base + ` [검토자 코멘트] ${comment} 위 코멘트 내용을 최대한 반영해서 작성해줘.` : base; })() }] }) }}

nodes.name: Claude Draft
nodes.notes: References 'Build News Summary' by name (not $json) because $json here is the Wait node's resumed payload, not the news summary.

nodes.name: Search Pexels Image
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: get a free API key at https://www.pexels.com/api/ and paste it into the Authorization header (raw key, no 'Bearer' prefix). Query comes directly from Claude's image_keywords (content-relevant, not just category) -- see Claude Draft's prompt. alwaysOutputData=true so a zero-result search doesn't skip the rest of the publish chain.

nodes.name: IF Image Found
nodes.notes: false branch (no Pexels result) skips straight to Finalize Featured Media with featured_media left at 0 -- a missing image must never block publishing the post itself.

nodes.name: Upload Image to WordPress
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: reconnect the 'Gabia' Basic Auth credential like the other WordPress nodes. Uploads the downloaded binary directly to the media library; response's 'id' becomes the post's featured_media.

nodes.name: Search WP Category
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: reconnect the 'Gabia' Basic Auth credential (Application Password) -- this and the other new WordPress HTTP nodes all need it reselected after import. The User-Agent header is the confirmed fix for the 401 that blocked auto-publishing -- do not remove it. alwaysOutputData=true (Settings tab) is required: an empty search result ([]) would otherwise make n8n skip every downstream node entirely.

nodes.name: Create WP Category
nodes.notes: Only runs when Search WP Category found no exact match. Creates the category once; future runs with the same category name will find it via search instead.

nodes.name: Get All WP Tags
nodes.notes: Fetches all existing tags once (up to 100) -- matching against Claude's tags array happens in the next Code node, same fetch-all-then-filter pattern used elsewhere in this workflow. Both the 'found' (true) and 'not found' (false) branches of IF Category Found lead here. alwaysOutputData=true (Settings tab) required on a fresh site with zero tags.

nodes.name: Create WP Tag
nodes.notes: Runs once per missing tag (one item per tag from Resolve Tag IDs), creating each new tag in WordPress.

nodes.name: Aggregate Tag IDs
nodes.notes: Collapses however many items arrived (0 from the false branch's single passthrough item with no id, or N created-tag items from the true branch) into exactly one downstream execution -- avoids Publish WordPress firing multiple times.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ title: $('Parse Claude Response').first().json.title, content: $('Parse Claude Response').first().json.body_html, excerpt: $('Parse Claude Response').first().json.excerpt, status: "draft", categories: [(() => { const norm = $('Normalize Category Search').first().json; if (norm.found) return norm.id; try { return $('Create WP Category').first().json.id; } catch (e) { return null; } })()], tags: $('Finalize Tag IDs').first().json.tag_ids, featured_media: $('Finalize Featured Media').first().json.featured_media }) }}

nodes.name: Publish WordPress
nodes.notes: The User-Agent: curl/8.21.0 header is the confirmed fix for the 401 rest_cannot_create error that blocked this for weeks -- do not remove it. Publishes as status=draft so final polish can be added in wp-admin before actually going live. featured_media comes from the Pexels chain above (0 if no image was found).

nodes.name: Mark Handled
nodes.notes: Now records the real wp_post_id from Publish WordPress, restoring the column's original purpose from before the email fallback.
